main_status_string_bindings.text: Theta transformation laws fix the additive constant, division identities control the norm, and the local-height product formula fixes its arithmetic normalization.
Integral centralizers, finite norm maps and cusp winding determine the parameter equivalence, while the marked reflection and cap-meridian maps determine the real forms.
The integral congruence kernel determines the parabolic quotient, and the wedge equation with its Hermitian form determines the fibre strata.

Root characters and logarithmic residues compute the connecting scalar and direct images, exterior quotients by $dt$ give the ordinary modules, and theta factors with cusp Cartier frames give the coefficient cocycles.
Weighted section counts and local Koszul modules compute every Picard twist, while the nonzero Kodaira--Spencer class gives the coordinate on the Kuranishi line.

The intrinsic canonical system recovers the marked base, finite-orbit vanishing kills horizontal meridians, and their constant ratio across the connected compact corner contradicts the nonzero cusp coefficient.
The intrinsic Albanese invariant detects the outer boundary, and the exact dual-period equations with their quadratic cancellation determine nonseparation and every marked closed-group limit.
New period evaluations, norm values and level classification, using the elliptic section of \cite[Remark~3.12, p.~19]{AC2026}.
New classification for the displayed discrete data and real forms; the standard $2\mathbb Z$ equivalence is known \cite[Theorem~1.4, p.~3]{DuEtAl2026v1}.
New integral monodromy and maximal proper domain, answering \cite[Remark~8.4, pp.~23--24]{Engel2026}.
New evaluated cohomology and coefficient atlas; the ordinary-module calculation corrects \cite[Remark~9.21, p.~81]{AC2026}.
New all-twist and higher-multiplicity formulas; the standard untwisted deformation results are known \cite[Theorem~6.12, pp.~81--82; Proposition~6.16, p.~85]{DuEtAl2026v1}.
New filling obstruction and untwisted plumbing; the Euler calculation corrects the proposed central model in \cite[Conjecture~8.2, p.~22]{Engel2026}.
New boundary obstruction and marked limit formulas, using the annihilator duality of \cite[Theorem~3.1, p.~2017]{Cornulier2011}.

New explicit evaluations and sharp norm bounds from the known section \cite[Remark~3.12, p.~19]{AC2026}; the quotient and height inputs are \cite[Definition~2.3, p.~5; proof of Lemma~2.1, pp.~3--4]{Engel2026}, transported by \cref{I:weierstrass-comparison}.

New discrete-data and real-form extensions of the standard equivalence \cite[Theorem~1.4, p.~3]{DuEtAl2026v1}; the higher construction is \cite[Theorem~1.1, p.~1; Section~2.1, pp.~4--6]{ViaclovskyLog2026}, with $(k,l)=(1,1)$ giving the standard data.

New exact group, quotient and proper-domain answer to \cite[Remark~8.4, pp.~23--24]{Engel2026}; the fibre tests use the integral wedge equation of \cite[Lemma~9.2, p.~65]{AC2026} with the period row $\beta=\beta_c$.

New value of the Hodge integer, full cohomology and coefficient representatives extending \cite[Theorem~9.1(vi), p.~65; Proposition~9.20, p.~80]{AC2026}; the degree-one cusp module corrects its Remark~9.21, p.~81, and specifies the degree dependence of Remark~1.3, p.~5.

New Picard-twist and coprime-root calculations extending the known standard tangent, Kuranishi and automorphism results \cite[Theorems~1.3--1.4, p.~3; Theorem~6.12, pp.~81--82; Proposition~6.16, p.~85; Theorem~7.14, p.~95]{DuEtAl2026v1}, under the parameter map of \cref{night:P5.7}.

New marked nonfilling obstruction and explicit untwisted filling in the degeneration setting of \cite[Remark~8.1, p.~22]{Engel2026}; virtual Euler number zero excludes the particular central model in its Conjecture~8.2, p.~22.

New intrinsic boundary and marked additive-limit calculations; the map $w\mapsto iw/216$ supplies the modular boundary, and \cite[Theorem~3.1, p.~2017]{Cornulier2011} supplies closed-group duality under the real annihilator map.

duplicate_scope_witnesses_verified_uncha.exact_text:
For the elliptic-quartic configuration of \ref{push:src:B.4.10}, the three
pairwise normal-line products, including the triple-curve factors,
can consequently all be made trivial using
\[
 A=\operatorname{Bl}_E\PP^3,\qquad
 B=S\times\PP^1,\qquad C=\mathcal V.
\]
Here $C$ is the constructed proper surface family over an open
disc. Its continuous surjection onto that disc proves that $C$ is
noncompact.

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 \text{double surface}&
 N_{D/\text{first branch}}\otimes
 N_{D/\text{second branch}}\otimes\OO_D(\text{triple curve})\\ \hline
 E\times\PP^1&
 (L\boxtimes\OO(-1))\otimes(L^{-1}\boxtimes\OO)
       \otimes(\OO_E\boxtimes\OO(1))=\OO\\
 Q&\OO_Q\otimes K_Q\otimes\OO_Q(E)=\OO_Q\\
 S&\OO_S\otimes\OO_S(-E)\otimes\OO_S(E)=\OO_S.
\end{array}
\]
The three displayed evaluation maps are the required pairwise
normal-line trivializations. The third space maps surjectively and
properly to an open disc, which proves its noncompactness.
